flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:73:
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:74:    Example::
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:75:
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:76:      model_pk =  [ColumnA, ColumnB]
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:77:      ids = ((1,2), (1,3))
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:78:
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:79:      tuple_operator(model_pk, ids) -> or_( and_( ColumnA == 1, ColumnB == 2), and_( ColumnA == 1, ColumnB == 3) )
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:80:
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:81:    The returning operator can be used within a filter(), as it is just an or_ operator
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:82:    """
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:83:    ands = []
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:84:    for id in ids:
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:85:        k = []
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:86:        for i in range(len(model_pk)):
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:87:            k.append(eq(model_pk[i], id[i]))
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:88:        ands.append(and_(*k))
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:89:    if len(ands) >= 1:
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:90:        return or_(*ands)
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:91:    else:
flask_admin/contrib/sqla/tools.py:92:        return None
